If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `testDistributionClone` attempts to verify that cloning a distribution by serialization (using `deepClone`) yields an identical random sample sequence after cloning. The test reseeds the RNG of the original distribution, samples from it, then clones it by serialization and deserialization, and checks if the cloned distribution produces the same sample as the original.

The issue report points out that cloning GammaDistribution fails this expectation, i.e., the cloned distribution does not produce the same random samples. Investigating the inheritance chain, GammaDistribution inherits from AbstractRealDistribution, which has a `random` field of type `RandomGenerator`. This is initialized with Well19937c, which in turn inherits from AbstractWell, which implements Serializable.

The root cause seems to be that while the RNG state is serialized, Well19937c inherits state from AbstractWell that does not completely or correctly serialize and deserialize the RNG internal state. Code inspection of AbstractWell reveals internal state variables (e.g., int array `v` and index) that represent the state of the RNG. The constructor initializes these states with the seed, and `setSeed` initializes the state and clears the cache. However, the bug report hints that deserializing does not properly restore or reconstruct this state, likely because `AbstractWell` does not implement custom serialization methods (`writeObject` and `readObject`) to explicitly persist the RNG internal state.

Thus, the serialization/deserialization of the RNG internal state is broken or incomplete, resulting in the cloned distribution having a different RNG internal state and producing different samples post-cloning.

This explains why the distribution clone test fails: the cloned distribution is not a proper deep clone preserving RNG state, breaking the reproducibility guarantee for tests requiring deterministic sequences.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
